_comment: Daily map events (PLAN.md). Hours are game hours (divided by world speed). Every `everyHours` from the start of a run (the first after its first day), an event rises on passable open land `range.min` to `range.max` hexes from one of the players' villages, and goes after `lastsHours` unless an army is already on its way to it. `kinds` are picked by weight. captives: a camp (kind 'captives') of `guards` of the land's front, more each day (x 1 + `growthPerDay` x (day - 1)), holding captives: freeing them (clearing the camp) brings, with chance `unitsChance`, `count` (+ `countPerDay` a day) of one of `units` into the army that freed them, or else `resources` (x 1 + `growthPerDay` x (day - 1)) carried home with it; it doesn't grow, join hordes or ambush caravans. ruin: a hard ancient site (sites.json) watched by `guardianFactor` times its usual guardians, whose resources are worth `lootFactor` times as much. shipyard: a group project on a river bank (a hex beside a river edge): any player sends resources from a village within `range` hexes until `cost` is paid (if nobody has sent anything when its time is up, it goes); then the boat takes `buildHours` to build, and every `raidEveryHours` raiders (`raiders` of the land's front, more each day like the captives' guards) strike it in `raiderStance`: armies standing on its hex defend it one after another, and if they don't drive them off, `setbackHours` of work are lost. When the boat is done, armies, caravans and scouts stepping between two hexes beside that river (every river edge joined to the one it was built on) move `laneSpeed` times as fast, for good; a lake the river reaches is sailed too (its hexes, at a move cost of `lakeMoveCost` before the lane's speed, its shores, and the rivers flowing into it join the lane), though no army can stop on a lake. Every event done brings a bounty, `reward.resources` (x 1 + `reward.growthPerDay` x (day of the run - 1)), to the first village of whoever did it (captives freed, a ruin searched); a finished boat brings it to every member. An event left undone when its time is up (captives taken away, a ruin nobody searched, a shipyard nobody paid into) makes the next horde of its front (the land it rose in, or the first active one) hate the more: `failure.hatred` added to its hatred (horde.json). Each is told to the players as an event notice, which the game shows in a popup.
